title: Magnetism in a homometallic square-planar Cu$({\mathrm{II})}$$_4$Cu$({\mathrm{II})}$ metallacrown
authors: Luca Bischof, Ariyan Tavakoli, Sascha Pietruska, Lena Spillecke, Ina Heckelmann, Changhyun Koo, Luca M. Carrella, Eva Rentschler, Hans Christian Schneider, Rüdiger Klingeler
abstract: The well-established homometallic metallacrown Cu(II)[12-MC$_\text{Cu(II)N(Shi)}$-4]$^{2-}$, comprising four square-planarly arranged Cu(II) ions surrounding a slightly off-plane central Cu(II) ion, provides an excellent platform for investigating magnetism in exchange-coupled Cu(II) clusters both by experimental and ab initio numerical methods. In the present work, sterically bulky substituents are introduced into the salicylhydroxamate ligand to obtain a modified derivative, Cu$({\mathrm{II})}$[12-MC$_\text{Cu$({\mathrm{II})}$N(L)}$-4]$^{2-}$ (Cu$_4$Cu), thereby effectively suppressing intermolecular magnetic interactions and enabling a detailed investigation of its intrinsic ground-state spin structure and exchange interactions. Static magnetization reveals competing antiferromagnetic exchange interactions of $J_1=-8.1(2)$ THz ($-33.5(8)$ meV) between the central and the peripheral sites and $J_2=-4.40(12)$ THz ($-18.2(5)$ meV) between neighboring sites on the ring of the metallacrown, which are corroborated by ab initio broken symmetry-based density functional theory (DFT). These couplings yield an $S=1/2$ ground state for Cu$_4$Cu at low temperatures, for which X-band and high-frequency/high-field electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) precisely determine the $g$-factors $g_x = 2.028$, $g_y = 2.056$, and $g_z = 2.222$ close to axial anisotropy and in agreement with our DFT results. The ground-state spin-configuration is characterized by $d_{xy}$-character of the unoccupied states. Furthermore, our magnetization data evidence thermal transitions across a doublet-to-quartet gap of $Δ_{1/2\rightarrow3/2} = 4.8(4)$ THz which is also indicated by the emergence of an excited-state EPR signal.
summary: This work investigates the magnetism of a modified homometallic $	ext{Cu}_4	ext{Cu}$ metallacrown, using bulky substituents to isolate the intrinsic magnetic unit. By combining static magnetization, high-frequency EPR, and DFT, the authors determined competing antiferromagnetic exchange couplings and confirmed an $S=1/2$ ground state. The results provide precise spectroscopic parameters ($g$-factors and energy gaps) essential for understanding spin dynamics in molecular quantum materials.
main_problem: The study aims to investigate the intrinsic ground-state spin structure and exchange interactions within a modified homometallic metallacrown ($	ext{Cu}_4	ext{Cu}$) to understand its magnetic behavior.
main_result: The system exhibits an $S=1/2$ ground state characterized by competing antiferromagnetic exchange couplings ($J_1$ and $J_2$), which are corroborated by both magnetization and DFT calculations.
method: The research combines static magnetization measurements, high-frequency Electron Paramagnetic Resonance (EPR) spectroscopy, and *ab initio* Density Functional Theory (DFT) calculations.
model_or_system: The physical system is the $	ext{Cu}_4	ext{Cu}$ metallacrown, featuring five $	ext{Cu(II)}$ ions. The magnetic behavior is modeled using an effective Heisenberg spin Hamiltonian incorporating two primary exchange interactions, $J_1$ and $J_2$.
key_observables: Ground state spin ($S=1/2$), exchange couplings ($J_1 = -8.1 	ext{ THz}$, $J_2 = -4.40 	ext{ THz}$), anisotropic $g$-factors ($g_x, g_y, g_z$), and thermal transition gaps ($\Delta_{1/2	o 3/2} = 4.8 	ext{ THz}$).
important_parameters: Low temperatures (2–10 K), magnetic fields up to 7 T, and characteristic energy scales in the THz range.
main_assumptions: The DFT calculations utilize a broken symmetry approach, and the magnetic model relies on fitting the Heisenberg Hamiltonian to experimental $\chi T$ data.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the crystal structure and magnetic coupling model, and the paper discusses spin-resolved projected density of states (pDOS) for both $	ext{Cu}$ $3d$ and ligand $p$-orbitals.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the physical system and the need to suppress intermolecular interactions via ligand modification. It then presents evidence from static susceptibility and magnetization fitting to determine exchange couplings ($J_1, J_2$). Finally, it uses high-field EPR and DFT to confirm the $S=1/2$ ground state, determine anisotropic $g$-factors, and characterize excited state transitions.
why_interesting: The detailed characterization of magnetic exchange pathways ($J_1, J_2$) and the determination of anisotropic $g$-factors using high-field EPR provide quantitative insights into spin-orbit coupling and magnetic anisotropy in molecular magnets, which is crucial for quantum information applications.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Top view of (a) the crystal structure and (b) the central molecular motif and magnetic couplings of Cu4Cu. In (a), a single complex is shown consisting of four repetition units [Cu–N–O] with ligand L. The crystal packing is shown in the SM [14]. The magnetic model in (b) is sketched with couplings as arrows indicating isotropic magnetic interactions between the central Cu(II) moment and its neighbors with coupling strength J1 (green), and between neighboring outer Cu(II) moments with coupling strength J2 (black). Ions and bonds coloring: Cu (blue), O (red), N (light blue), Si (green), C (brown), and H (white).

FIG. 2. Temperature dependence of the static magnetic sus- ceptibility measured at B = 0.1 T on a fixed powder sample is plotted as χT. The red solid line shows the best fit of the spin hamiltonian Eq. 1 with the parameters described in the main text. Further lines display the simulated χT curves with the magnetic exchange couplings J1, J2 calculated by PBE0 (blue) and CAM-B3LYP (green) as described in Sec. IV. In- set: Isothermal magnetization at low temperatures from 2 K to 10 K with a temperature increment of 1 K between the curves. The red solid line shows the fit of the Brillouin func- tion Eq. 2 to the data at T = 2 K.

FIG. 3. X-band EPR spectra of fixed powder sample of CuII[12-MCCuII-4] at (a) low and (b) intermediate temper- atures exhibit the strong low-temperature resonance line s1 and the thermally-induced feature s2. Note different ordi- nates in (a) and (b) such that the spectrum at 33 K is the least intense spectrum in (a) and the most intense spectrum in (b).

FIG. 4. Fitting of the X-band EPR spectra showing (a) the low-temperature signal s1 at T = 6.3 K and (b) the thermally- induced resonance line s2 at T = 95.9 K. Solid red lines show the best fits to the data based on an S = 1/2 spin model with anisotropic g-factors, line broadening and hyperfine interac- tion (only b) as described in the main text. The resulting spin Hamiltonian parameters are summarized in Tab. I.

FIG. 5. High-frequency/high-field EPR spectra of Cu4Cu at T = 2 K exhibit the low-temperature EPR signal s1. Solid black lines describe the best simultaneous fit to the three transmission spectra with microwave frequencies around 100 GHz, which yields the g-factors discussed in the main text.
